keyVerseText: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective οἰκεῖος (oikeîos) derives from the root word οἶκος (oîkos), which means 'home' or 'household.' This origin emphasizes a connection to a specific dwelling or family unit, extending beyond a mere physical structure to include the people and relationships within it. The root sense conveys intimacy and belonging, highlighting not just any association but one grounded in shared home and kinship, which enriches the English gloss of 'household' with a deeper familial and domestic nuance.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, οἰκεῖος appears a total of three times, consistently conveying the idea of those who belong to a particular household or family. Its top translations—'them who are of the household,' 'of the household,' and 'for those of his own house'—reflect this stable semantic field. This consistency reveals that the term not only identifies physical or familial relations but also extends metaphorically to spiritual kinship, as seen in usages tied to faith communities or God's family.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, understanding οἰκεῖος as those 'of the household' enriches our grasp of the biblical concept of family, both natural and spiritual. It underscores the intimate bonds that unite believers as members of God's household, moving beyond mere external association to a deep relational identity. This word reminds Christians that faith creates a new family bound by shared life in Christ, emphasizing responsibility, care, and mutual support within the community. Recognizing this term's root meaning helps believers appreciate their belonging in God's family as a profound and personal reality, not simply a doctrinal category.
keyVerseReflection: Galatians 6:10 exhorts believers to do good to all people, but especially to 'them who are of the household of faith.' The use of οἰκεῖος here highlights the special obligation Christians have toward those who share their spiritual home. It calls attention to the familial nature of the faith community, urging care and kindness first to those intimately connected within the family of God. This word deepens the verse's appeal by framing Christian love as a natural extension of belonging to God's household.
